spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Once the derivative-side data are fixed, the mean-square constant becomes a quadratic functional of the mollifier profile P. Euler-Lagrange turns its optimization into a two-point linear ODE, and integration by parts compresses the optimum to boundary data.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The extracted functional contains integrals of |P′|², P′P, and |P|² with coefficients A, B, and C formed from an auxiliary w. Its minimizer satisfies A P″−(B−conjugate(B))P′−C P=0 with P(0)=0 and P(1)=1. The exponential-form solution is substituted back, and the source notes that it can be uniformly approximated by admissible polynomials.
directed.conceptual_reading: A discrete coefficient search is relaxed to a continuous boundary-value problem. The ODE exposes the optimal shape rather than searching polynomial coefficients blindly.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The mean-square main term becomes a quadratic variational functional, then a boundary-value ODE, then an explicit boundary expression used in the proportion estimate.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The exact definitions and solution formula are partially damaged, and the continuous minimizer is not itself a polynomial. Approximation recovers admissibility, but this is not a claim of global joint optimality over P, Q, R, and θ.
directed.uncertainty: Moderate for the variational mechanism and displayed ODE; high for exact coefficients and closed-form normalization.
